EMPIRICAL RESEARCH PLAN  

--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy  
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Primary strategy: Geographic (border) regression-discontinuity design (GRD).  

Rationale  
• The land–revenue system changes discretely at historically drawn district (and sometimes taluk) borders.  
• Borders were fixed in the early 19th century by British administrators for idiosyncratic military-political reasons, not agro-climatic ones.  
• Within a narrow corridor that straddles each historical border, agro-climatic conditions, market access, and post-Independence state policies are plausibly smooth, so any sharp change in long-run outcomes can be attributed to the discontinuous change in property-rights institutions.  
• GRD provides a transparent causal estimate while remaining agnostic about functional form farther away from the cutoff.  

Supplementary designs (robustness only)  
(a) Difference-in-differences on the sub-sample where colonial-era yield data exist (pre- vs post-Independence).  
(b) 2-stage least squares using “year of first British conquest × ideology of first Collector” as an instrument for the landlord dummy, to address attenuation from mis-classification in fuzzy borders.  

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control  
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable:  
Treated = 1 if the historical land-revenue system in the district (or sub-district) was landlord-based (zamindari or malguzari) at the time of the first permanent settlement; 0 otherwise (raiyatwari or mahalwari).

Control group:  
Districts (or sub-districts) lying on the other side of the same historical border but within the chosen GRD bandwidth serve as counterfactuals.

Timing / event date:  
Treatment was assigned once—between 1793 and 1860—so the “event” precedes all outcome measurement periods (1956–1991). Because the treatment is time-invariant, we implement a cross-sectional GRD.

Running variable and cutoff:  
Running variable r = signed great-circle distance (in km) from the district centroid to the nearest historical landlord/non-landlord border segment.  
Cutoff = 0 at the border (r < 0 for landlord side, r > 0 for non-landlord side).  
Estimation is local: |r| ≤ h, where h is selected by rdrobust’s MSE-optimal algorithm and verified with ±50 km and ±100 km fixed windows.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
--------------------------------------------------------------------
A1. Continuity of potential outcomes: In the absence of treatment, the conditional expectation of outcomes varies smoothly with distance from the border.  
Plausibility: Borders followed administrative expediency, not terrain or soil lines; we will test for continuity in rainfall, soil, altitude, pre-colonial population, and distance to railways.

A2. No manipulation / sorting: Districts could not strategically locate themselves on one side of a border set 150–200 years ago.  
Plausibility: Very high—political boundaries were imposed by the colonial state.

A3. SUTVA / limited spillovers within bandwidth: Outcomes in one district are not driven by the treatment status of its neighbour once we focus on a ≤100 km window.  
Plausibility: Some market spillovers may exist; we will show results are stable when the window is narrowed to 50 km and when border-pair fixed effects are added.

A4. Unique treatment discontinuity: No other policy jumps exactly at the same border.  
Plausibility: Possible concern because some borders coincide with old princely/state boundaries; we will control for pre-1947 province fixed effects and check that literacy, roads, and revenue expenditure in 1911 do not jump at the cutoff.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation  
--------------------------------------------------------------------
T1. Confounding historical borders (e.g., linguistic or princely-state lines)  
• Mitigation: Include province-pair fixed effects; test continuity of 1901 census literacy and population density; perform placebo GRDs at alternative (rotated) border lines.

T2. Spatial spillovers or measurement error in centroid distance  
• Mitigation: (i) Restrict bandwidth; (ii) use border-pair matched-pair estimator (difference within each nearest-neighbour pair); (iii) implement Conley spatial HAC errors.

T3. Heterogeneous post-Independence state policies across states  
• Mitigation: State fixed effects in all specifications; sub-sample analyses within the four largest states; interact state dummies with distance polynomial.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline  
--------------------------------------------------------------------
```r
# 0. Packages -------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table); library(sf); library(fixest); library(rdrobust)

# 1. Load Data ------------------------------------------------------
dist <- fread("district_level_data.csv")          # outcomes & controls
borders <- st_read("landsystem_borders.shp")      # polyline of historical border
district_shp <- st_read("district_centroids.shp") # centroid geometry

# 2. Merge shapefiles + compute running variable -------------------
dist <- merge(dist, district_shp, by = "dist_id")
# Signed distance: negative if landlord side
dist$landlord <- as.integer(dist$system %in% c("zamindari","malguzari"))
dist <- st_as_sf(dist)                     # make sf object for geometry ops
dist$r <- st_distance(dist, borders) %>%   # min distance
          as.numeric() / 1000              # metres→km
# Need sign:
dist$side <- st_nearest_feature(dist, borders, returnDist = FALSE)
dist$border_system <- borders$system[dist$side]
dist$r <- ifelse(dist$landlord==1, -dist$r, dist$r)

# 3. Keep observations in chosen bandwidth -------------------------
bw <- 100                                # km
local <- dist[abs(r) <= bw, ]

# 4. Main GRD regression (local linear) ----------------------------
m1 <- rdrobust(y = local$irrigated_share,
               x = local$r,
               covs = cbind(local$rainfall, local$soil_quality, local$altitude),
               fuzzy = NULL, cluster = local$prov_border_id)

print(summary(m1))

# 5. Parametric alternative with fixest ----------------------------
m2 <- feols(irrigated_share ~ landlord + poly(r,2) + rainfall + soil_quality + altitude |
            state_id , data = local, cluster = "prov_border_id")
etable(m2, cluster = "prov_border_id")

# 6. Robustness: narrower bandwidth & placebo ----------------------
# (a) 50-km window
local50 <- local[abs(r) <= 50, ]
m3 <- feols(irrigated_share ~ landlord + poly(r,2) + rainfall + soil_quality + altitude |
            state_id , data = local50, cluster = "prov_border_id")
# (b) Fake border 50 km north (shift)
borders_fake <- st_shift(borders, 0, 50000)  # 50 km in metres
# Re-compute fake running variable and repeat; expect 0 effect
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results  
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Sign: Landlord history → lower current agricultural investment and productivity, weaker human-capital outcomes.  
Magnitude (order-of-magnitude priors):  
• Irrigated share: –10 p.p. (≈ –20 % relative to sample mean of 0.50)  
• HYV adoption: –8 p.p.  
• Crop yields: –75 kg/ha for rice (≈ –12 %)  
• Literacy: –5 p.p.  
• Infant mortality: +8 deaths per 1,000 live births  

Underlying mechanism prior: landlord areas suffered persistently lower public goods due to unequal wealth distribution and weaker local political voice.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (Spatial RDD)  
--------------------------------------------------------------------
C1. Covariates change smoothly at cutoff: 1  
C2. No manipulation of running variable: 1  
C3. Precise knowledge of cutoff & treatment assignment: 1  
C4. Appropriate bandwidth & functional-form diagnostics: 0.5 (subject to robustness)  
C5. Placebo & falsification tests implemented: 1  

Total = 4.5 / 5 – cautiously credible.
